title: 👑 Elite Challenge: Master of Future Forms

questions.prompt: Choose the sentence where EVERY verb form is correct:

options.text: I intend to studying abroad and I'm thinking of getting a loan.
I intend to study abroad and I'm thinking to get a loan.
I intend to study abroad and I'm thinking of getting a loan.
I intends to study abroad and I'm thinking of getting a loan.

questions.explanation: Both structures are right only in "I intend to study abroad and I'm thinking of getting a loan": intend to + base verb (study), be thinking of + verb + ing (getting). "intend to studying" puts -ing after to; "thinking to get" borrows the to of intend; "I intends" adds -s with I.

questions.prompt: Complete Yasmine's answer: "Where will you live in Germany?" — "I ___ with my cousin."
questions.explanation: be thinking of + verb + ing, with am for I: I am thinking of living with my cousin. "thinking of to live" mixes the two structures; "thinking to live" replaces of with the to of intend; "thinking of living" without am drops the verb be.

questions.prompt: Which utterance expresses a PLANNED ACTION in the future?

options.text: I'm thinking of writing a short story.
I intend to visit my uncle.
I'm going to visit my uncle.

questions.explanation: I'm visiting my uncle tomorrow = am + verb + ing + the future word tomorrow: a planned action. "I'm thinking of writing" is also am + -ing, but it expresses an intention and has no future word; "intend to visit" and "going to visit" are intentions too.

questions.prompt: Complete the scientist's prediction (no petrol, only the sun): "In 2050, cars ___ on petrol; they ___ solar power."
questions.explanation: The future tense is will / won't + bare infinitive, and the context says no petrol, only the sun: cars won't run on petrol; they will use solar power. "will run … won't use" is correct grammar but says the opposite of the context; "will uses" adds -s after will; "don't run" is the simple present, not the future.

questions.prompt: Find the error: "Tomorrow I am meeting my coach, and next month I am going to joining the national team."
questions.explanation: The error is "am going to joining": be going to is followed by a base verb — I am going to join the national team. "Tomorrow I am meeting" is a correct planned action (present progressive + future word), and "next month" and "the national team" are correct too.

questions.prompt: Turn it into a planned-action question with the future word given: "Is Dora going to finish her studies?" (next year)

options.text: Does Dora finish her studies next year?
Is Dora finish her studies next year?
Is Dora finishing her studies next year?
Will Dora finishing her studies next year?

questions.explanation: A planned action in a question keeps is + verb + ing + the future word, with is before the subject: Is Dora finishing her studies next year? "Does Dora finish" is the simple present; "Is Dora finish" loses the -ing; "Will Dora finishing" puts -ing after will, which needs a bare infinitive.
